references.text: Abraham's hospitality: he offers water to wash the guests' feet, a parallel to the action of Joseph's steward.
Laban's servant gives water for foot washing and fodder for the camels – a close parallel to the hospitality shown in Joseph's house.
Lot offers hospitality to the angels, including foot washing, as part of the custom of receiving travelers.
The old man takes in the traveling Levite, washes their feet, and provides fodder for the donkeys – very similar to the situation in Gen 43:24.
Jesus points out that the host did not give him water for his feet, in contrast to the hospitality shown in Genesis.
Jesus washes the disciples' feet, an action that reflects the ancient custom of hospitality involving foot washing.
Contrast between the brothers' fear that their donkeys will be taken and Joseph's hospitality, which provides fodder for them.
